title: Schäfer Lab
text:
We explore quantum phenomena in fields like surface science and heterogeneous catalysis by developing and applying scalable wavefunction based algorithms to solve the many-body Schrödinger equation with high accuracy.
We aim to enhance the synergy between experimental and computational approaches by addressing key limitations in state-of-the art computational methods. Our research contributes to the broader goal of developing new functional materials to aid the crucial transition to greener and more efficient industrial processes.

title: Congratulations to Francesco Mereto
text:
Francesco Mereto successfully passed his Master’s exam about Virtual Orbital Space Compression via Davidson-Based techniques.





In his thesis, he developed enhanced Davidson algorithms to significantly speed up compression techniques of the virtual orbital space starting from the unbiased plane wave basis. This is particularly useful for correlation workflows (e.g., coupled cluster theory) applied to systems which include a lot of vacuum.

title: Publication in Nature Communications
text:
Understanding discrepancies in noncovalent interaction energies from wavefunction theories for large molecules





Our paper on noncovalent interactions is now published in Nature Communications. We investigate why two of the most trusted methods in quantum chemistry, CCSD(T) and DMC, have shown puzzling disagreements for large molecules. We identify an issue in the standard CCSD(T) method and show how our CCSD(cT) approach fixes this.
